Metricool: scheduled Wed 2026-10-21 13:00 IG + TikTok
Carousel 1312: stop asking which AI is best. Claude builds, GPT gets one job. CTA: comment AI. Drive: Carousels/1312-claude-gpt-one-job/house
guide: Use one AI model to build your app and a second, cheaper one for a single narrow job, instead of hunting for the "best" AI. You need Claude Code (or ChatGPT / Codex), an OpenAI API key and a small project to build.
1. Pick the one job your app needs an AI to do at run time, such as summarising a message or tagging an email.
1. Open Claude Code and have it build the app itself: the screens, the database and the glue between them.
1. Create an API key on the OpenAI platform and keep it in your host's environment settings, not in your code.
1. Ask Claude Code to add one function that sends the input to a GPT model with a short instruction and returns a fixed, structured answer.
1. Keep GPT out of everything else, so the rest of the app never depends on a model's judgement.
1. Deploy the app on Vercel, with Supabase for the data if you need a database.
1. Test the single GPT call with ten real inputs and tighten the instruction until the answers stay consistent.
Watch out: do not give one model every job; Claude builds the app, GPT gets one defined task, and a vague task is where the answers go wrong.

```
You are my senior developer. Build a small web app that does <what the app does> for <who uses it>.
Tools I have: Claude Code or ChatGPT (Codex), an OpenAI API key, a Vercel account and optionally a Supabase project.
Requirements:
- You write the whole app: pages, data storage and the glue between them.
- Add exactly one AI feature: <the single job, e.g. "tag each incoming message as urgent, normal or low">. Put it in one function that calls a GPT model with a short, fixed instruction and returns a structured answer (JSON with a small set of allowed values).
- No other part of the app may depend on a model's output. If the call fails or returns something invalid, fall back to a safe default and log the error.
- Read the API key from an environment variable. Never put it in the code or in the repository.
- Deploy to Vercel and give me the environment variable names to set.
Return: the project structure, the code for each file, the instruction text you send to the model, and ten example inputs with expected outputs so I can test the AI call before launch. Ask me before you assume anything about <my data or workflow>.
```
